title: Tenant fencing & surge protection for Dedicated capacity (PRD)
creator: Lena Thompson
description: Problem: Tenants on Dedicated pools occasionally cause noisy neighbor effects during short high-traffic spikes. Existing soft-reservation and fairshare controls reduce long-term contention but allow transient surges that can breach per-tenant latency SLOs or force expensive fallbacks. Goal: introduce tenant fencing and a configurable surge-protection layer that enforces short-window burst policies, preemptive reclaim, and an emergency fence mode to protect critical reservations and SLOs while preserving benign burst behavior for bursty workloads.
goals: Provide a tenant-level fencing concept that can enforce strict isolation for reserved capacity during emergencies or planned maintenance
Ship a surge-protection policy framework: token-bucket-style burst allowance per tenant, time-windowed preemption, and elastic soft-burst accounting
Expose controls via API and Console: fence mode (off/soft/strict), burst_allowance (tokens/min), preemption_window (seconds), and fallback targets
Ensure observable signals and alerts: per-tenant breach events, preemption logs, latency/cost telemetry tied to fence events
Deliver clear acceptance criteria and migration plan with zero customer data loss and rollbacks
non_goals: Replace existing long-term autoscaling and reserved pool allocation logic (separate project)
Provide application-level QoS or per-request content inspection to determine priority
Support on-prem air-gapped installs in the first rollout (follow-up iteration will add packaging checklist)
requirements: Runtime: implement a tenant fencing state machine with states [open, soft_fence, strict_fence] and deterministic behavior under concurrent leases
Burst policy: per-tenant burst bucket with configurable capacity and refill rate; enforced across all hosts serving the tenant
Preemption: support graceful preemption with configurable grace period (default 10s) and fastest fallbacks that do not violate reserved tenant invariants
API: add endpoints to set/get tenant fence and burst policies (PATCH /v1/dedicated/tenants/{tenant_id}/policy)
Console: admin UI to view active fences, recent preemptions, and to toggle fence modes with justification notes and audit logging
Observability: emit events to tracing/logging that include tenant_id, fence_state, burst_usage_pct, preempted_request_ids, and affected_model_variant
SLA: under strict_fence, reserved tenants retain >= 99.95% of baseline p50/p95 latency compared to pre-fence baseline for the same request mix
Backwards compatibility: default behavior after rollout must match existing production semantics (no mandatory fences enabled), and API must be guarded by RBAC to admins and tenant-owners only
acceptance_criteria: Feature flags allow staged rollout: runtime flag enabled for 10% of clusters, then 50%, then all (documented toggle)
Unit and integration tests for fence state transitions and burst accounting covering edge cases under clock skew and node failures
E2E test demonstrating a simulated noisy neighbor spike where tenant A is soft_bursting and a strict_fence for tenant B preserves B's latency within target
API contract tests covering permissioning, validation errors for invalid policy values, and idempotency of PATCH operations
Console updates validated by design review: admin can set fence with a mandatory justification; audit log captures change and operator id
Telemetry: dashboards that surface per-tenant burst debt, preemptions per hour, and fence durations; alert rules created for >5 preemptions/min per pool
Canary metrics: when enabled in 10% of clusters, no increase in customer-facing 99th percentile latency or error rate beyond historical variance for 72h
Runbook updated: on-call playbook includes steps to disable strict_fence, revert policies, and escalation path if preemption causes regressions
success_metrics: Reduce incidents tied to transient noisy-neighbor latency violations on Dedicated pools by 60% within 90 days of full rollout
Limit emergency fallback usage for high-priority tenants by 75% during peak-day surges via strict_fence enforcement
Mean time to detect and resolve fence-induced regressions < 2 hours (measured from alert creation to mitigation action)
Adoption: 40% of enterprise customers with Dedicated pools have at least one tenant policy defined within 3 months
rollout_plan: 1) Implement runtime + API + lightweight console controls behind feature flags. 2) Enable on internal dogfooding clusters; run synthetic noisy-neighbor tests. 3) Canary to 10% production clusters for 72h; monitor dashboards and guardrails. 4) Gradually expand to 100% with post-mortem and automated rollback hooks. 5) Post-launch iterate on UI ergonomics and add advanced policies (time-boxed banked-credits) in follow-ups.
risks: Incorrect preemption logic could increase tail latency if not gradual; mitigation: conservative defaults and canary strategy
RBAC misconfiguration could expose fence controls; mitigation: require security review and enforce admin-only during early rollout
Customers relying on soft-burst behavior may see throttling; mitigation: communication plan and migration guidance
Cross-cluster coordination for burst buckets could be complex; mitigation: design for eventual consistency with windowed reconciliation
open_questions: Should burst_allowance be expressed in tokens per minute or as a percentage of pooled capacity? (tradeoffs: ease of reasoning vs fairness)
What is the default preemption grace period that balances user-perceived failure vs fast reclaim?
Do we need tenant-level audit retention > 1 year for compliance customers?
Is an automated fallback policy (auto-switch to smaller model variant) acceptable during strict_fence or should we force manual opt-in?
notes: PRD must be reviewed with Security and Legal before enabling strict_fence for regulated customers. Coordinate with Customer Success to prepare messaging and migration checklists for tenants that rely on burst behavior.
